questions.q: A 35-year-old male presents with a painless ulcer on the glans penis, with indurated, clean base and firm, non-tender inguinal lymphadenopathy. Dark-field microscopy shows motile spiral organisms. Which is the most appropriate treatment?
opts: Benzathine penicillin G 2.4 MU IM single dose
questions.exp: This is primary syphilis (Hunterian chancre). Benzathine penicillin G 2.4 MU IM single dose is first-line treatment for primary and secondary syphilis per WHO and IADVL guidelines.

questions.q: A 28-year-old HIV-positive patient (CD4 count 80 cells/μL) develops grouped vesicles on an erythematous base along the C5 dermatome. The lesions are unusually extensive. The most appropriate antiviral therapy is:
opts: Oral acyclovir 400 mg 5 times/day for 7 days
questions.exp: Disseminated/extensive herpes zoster in severely immunocompromised patients (CD4 <100) warrants IV acyclovir 10 mg/kg q8h due to risk of visceral dissemination and encephalitis. Oral therapy is insufficient in this setting.

questions.q: A 22-year-old presents with itchy, well-defined scaly plaques on the scalp with broken-off hair shafts, fluorescent green under Wood's lamp. KOH mount shows hair-shaft invasion. Which organism is responsible?
questions.exp: Microsporum canis causes ectothrix infection and bright green fluorescence under Wood's lamp. Trichophyton species cause endothrix infection with no fluorescence. Epidermophyton does not infect hair.

questions.q: A 45-year-old diabetic farmer develops a rapidly enlarging, crusted, erythematous plaque on the lower leg with undermined edges and necrotic base following a minor trauma. The most likely diagnosis is:
questions.exp: Meleney's synergistic gangrene (progressive bacterial synergistic gangrene) occurs in diabetics/immunocompromised following minor trauma, characterised by slow-spreading ulceration with undermined edges and characteristic zones of necrosis. It is caused by synergistic infection with microaerophilic streptococcus and Staphylococcus aureus.

questions.q: A leprosy patient on MDT develops sudden onset tender erythematous nodules on the face and extremities, fever, and iridocyclitis. The nerve involvement shows acute neuritis. This type of lepra reaction is:
questions.exp: Type 2 reaction (ENL) occurs in lepromatous and borderline lepromatous leprosy. Features include tender erythematous nodules, fever, systemic involvement (iridocyclitis, orchitis, neuritis). It is immune complex-mediated (Type III hypersensitivity). Treatment is thalidomide or prednisolone.

questions.q: A 60-year-old woman presents with tense bullae on normal and erythematous skin, predominantly on the trunk and flexures, with positive Nikolsky sign negative. ELISA shows IgG antibodies against BP180 and BP230. The diagnosis is:
questions.exp: Bullous pemphigoid is characterised by tense bullae, negative Nikolsky sign, IgG and C3 at the BMZ on DIF (linear), and ELISA positive for anti-BP180 (NC16A domain) and anti-BP230. It affects the elderly and targets hemidesmosomes.

questions.q: A 32-year-old woman presents with discoid skin lesions, photosensitivity, oral ulcers, and arthritis. ANA is positive (1:320, homogeneous), anti-dsDNA elevated, and C3/C4 low. She develops nephrotic syndrome. The most appropriate treatment for her systemic lupus erythematosus with nephritis is:
questions.exp: Lupus nephritis (Class III/IV) requires induction therapy with high-dose corticosteroids (prednisolone) plus mycophenolate mofetil (MMF) or cyclophosphamide. MMF is preferred for induction and maintenance due to equivalent efficacy and better tolerability.

questions.q: A 55-year-old male with chronic sun-damaged skin develops a firm, indurated, non-healing ulcer on the lower lip with everted edges and cervical lymphadenopathy. Biopsy shows islands of dysplastic squamous cells invading dermis with keratin pearls. The management is:
opts: Wide local excision with sentinel node biopsy
questions.exp: Squamous cell carcinoma of the lip with lymph node involvement (regional metastasis) requires wide local excision with adequate margins and sentinel lymph node biopsy or elective neck dissection. Lip SCC has higher metastatic potential than truncal SCC.

questions.q: A 40-year-old man presents with perifollicular haemorrhage, corkscrew hairs, and hyperkeratotic follicular papules on the lower limbs. He has a history of poor diet. Biopsy shows perifollicular haemorrhage and dilated follicles plugged with keratin. The deficiency responsible is:
questions.exp: Scurvy (Vitamin C deficiency) presents with perifollicular haemorrhage, corkscrew/swan-neck hairs, gingival changes, and poor wound healing. Vitamin C is essential for collagen synthesis and iron absorption. Keratosis pilaris-like follicular plugging is classic.

questions.q: During a patch test for allergic contact dermatitis, a patient shows a positive reaction at 48 and 96 hours with induration and vesiculation but not at 15 minutes. This represents:
questions.exp: Allergic contact dermatitis is a classic Type IV (T-cell mediated, delayed-type) hypersensitivity reaction. Reactions peak at 48-96 hours. Type I reactions occur within 15-20 minutes. The patch test specifically tests for type IV reactions.

questions.q: A 25-year-old presents with a 2 cm pearly, translucent nodule on the face with telangiectasia and a central ulcer with rolled, pearly edges. There is no regional lymphadenopathy. Dermoscopy shows arborising vessels. The most likely diagnosis is:
questions.exp: Nodular BCC presents as a pearly, translucent nodule with telangiectasia, rolled edges, and central ulceration ('rodent ulcer'). Arborising (tree-like) vessels on dermoscopy are pathognomonic. BCC rarely metastasises but locally destructive.

questions.q: A 19-year-old girl on oral isotretinoin for severe nodular acne develops severe headache, blurred vision, and papilloedema. What is the most likely adverse effect?
questions.exp: Pseudotumor cerebri (idiopathic intracranial hypertension) is a serious adverse effect of isotretinoin, especially when combined with tetracyclines. Presentation includes headache, tinnitus, papilloedema, and visual disturbances. Isotretinoin must be stopped immediately and tetracyclines avoided concurrently.

questions.q: A 38-year-old patient with leprosy on MDT (rifampicin, dapsone, clofazimine) develops sudden haemolysis with Heinz body formation, methaemoglobinaemia, and peripheral cyanosis. Which drug is responsible?
questions.exp: Dapsone causes dose-dependent haemolytic anaemia and methaemoglobinaemia, especially in G6PD-deficient patients. Heinz bodies (denatured Hb) are seen on peripheral smear. Methaemoglobinaemia causes cyanosis unresponsive to O2. Treatment: methylene blue IV.

questions.q: A 50-year-old woman with dermatomyositis develops proximal muscle weakness, heliotrope rash, Gottron's papules, V-sign, and shawl sign. Lab shows elevated CPK and aldolase. She should be screened for internal malignancy. The most common associated malignancy is:
questions.exp: Dermatomyositis in adults (especially >40 years) has strong paraneoplastic association. Ovarian carcinoma is most commonly associated in women with dermatomyositis. Nasopharyngeal carcinoma is most common overall in Asian populations. Malignancy search should be thorough.

questions.q: A 30-year-old presents with grouped pruritic vesicles on extensor surfaces of elbows, knees, and buttocks. DIF shows granular IgA deposits at dermal papillary tips. She also has malabsorption symptoms. The diagnosis and associated condition are:
opts: Linear IgA disease; associated with IgA nephropathy
Dermatitis herpetiformis; associated with coeliac disease
Bullous pemphigoid; associated with inflammatory bowel disease
Pemphigus herpetiformis; associated with internal malignancy
questions.exp: Dermatitis herpetiformis (Duhring's disease) presents with grouped pruritic vesicles on extensor surfaces. DIF shows granular IgA at papillary tips (pathognomonic). It is strongly associated with gluten-sensitive enteropathy (coeliac disease). Treatment: dapsone + gluten-free diet.

questions.q: A 27-year-old HIV-positive patient develops soft, painless, cauliflower-like perianal growths. DNA typing of the causative virus would most likely show:
questions.exp: Condylomata acuminata (anogenital warts) are caused by low-risk HPV types 6 and 11. High-risk types (16, 18, 31, 33) are associated with cervical and anogenital malignancies. HPV 8 is associated with epidermodysplasia verruciformis.

questions.q: A 45-year-old male presents with hypopigmented anaesthetic patches on the trunk, with loss of sensation to temperature, touch, and pain. Slit-skin smear is negative. Nerve biopsy shows granulomatous inflammation with epithelioid cells, Langhans giant cells, but no bacilli. This is classified as:
questions.exp: Tuberculoid leprosy (TT) features: few well-defined hypopigmented anaesthetic patches, negative SSS, strong CMI, granulomas with epithelioid cells and Langhans giant cells but no/very few bacilli. Classified as PB leprosy (1-5 patches). Treatment: rifampicin + dapsone for 6 months.

questions.q: A 16-year-old girl with a history of recurrent episodes of perioral, periorbital, and laryngeal swelling without urticaria or pruritus, triggered by stress and minor trauma. C4 is persistently low even between attacks. C1q is normal. The most likely diagnosis is:
questions.exp: Hereditary angioedema (HAE) due to C1-INH deficiency presents with recurrent non-pruritic, non-urticarial angioedema of skin and mucous membranes. C4 is persistently low (best screening test). C1q is normal (distinguishes from acquired form). Triggered by trauma, stress, oestrogens.

questions.q: A 55-year-old male smoker presents with multiple hyperkeratotic scaly plaques on sun-exposed areas of the face and dorsal hands. Some lesions show a cutaneous horn. Biopsy shows full-thickness epidermal dysplasia with loss of polarity but no basement membrane breach. This is:
questions.exp: Actinic keratosis (solar keratosis) shows partial-thickness epidermal dysplasia (unlike Bowen's disease which is full-thickness = SCCIS). Common in sun-exposed areas in fair-skinned individuals. Risk of progression to invasive SCC. Treatment: cryotherapy, topical 5-FU, imiquimod, PDT.

questions.q: A 22-year-old male presents with a painless ulcer with a 'clean punched-out' base and undermined edges on the shin after a tropical travel. No pain is noted despite the significant ulcer size. What is the most likely causative organism?
questions.exp: Buruli ulcer caused by Mycobacterium ulcerans is characterised by a painless, undermined ulcer, predominantly on the lower limbs. The mycobacterium produces mycolactone toxin causing cell necrosis. Treatment: rifampicin + clarithromycin (or amikacin) for 8 weeks.

questions.q: A 35-year-old woman develops a malar rash, photosensitivity, and discoid lesions. She is ANA positive with anti-Ro/SSA and anti-La/SSB antibodies. She is pregnant. The major concern for her neonate is:
opts: Neonatal lupus with congenital complete heart block
questions.exp: Anti-Ro/SSA and anti-La/SSB antibodies cross the placenta and can cause neonatal lupus syndrome. The most serious manifestation is congenital complete heart block (irreversible, may require pacemaker). Transient neonatal lupus rash can also occur. Fetal cardiac monitoring is essential.

questions.q: A 48-year-old presents with velvety, hyperpigmented, lichenified plaques in the axillae and back of the neck. She has a BMI of 38 and irregular menstrual cycles. Fasting blood sugar is 180 mg/dL. What is the most likely associated condition?
questions.exp: Acanthosis nigricans in an obese patient with hyperglycaemia is most commonly associated with insulin resistance and Type 2 diabetes. Insulin and IGF-1 bind to keratinocyte receptors causing epidermal proliferation. Malignant acanthosis nigricans (associated with GI adenocarcinoma) is more abrupt onset in non-obese elderly patients.

questions.q: A Mohs micrographic surgery is being planned for a skin tumour. Which of the following tumours is the BEST indication for Mohs surgery?
questions.exp: Mohs micrographic surgery offers highest cure rates with maximum tissue conservation for BCC and SCC at high-risk locations (face, H-zone), recurrent tumours, histologically aggressive subtypes, and poorly defined tumour borders. It is the gold standard for recurrent facial BCC.

questions.q: A 30-year-old woman presents with bluish-black pigmentation of fingernails, sclerae, and cartilaginous tissues (ears). Urine turns black on standing. The enzyme deficiency responsible is:
questions.exp: Ochronosis/alkaptonuria is caused by deficiency of homogentisate 1,2-dioxygenase (homogentisate oxidase), leading to accumulation of homogentisic acid which polymerises and deposits in connective tissues. Urine darkens on standing (alkalisation). Autosomal recessive.

questions.q: A 25-year-old woman with systemic sclerosis presents with Raynaud's phenomenon, sclerodactyly, calcinosis, telangiectasia, and dysphagia. Which antibody is most specific for this limited variant?
questions.exp: CREST syndrome (limited cutaneous systemic sclerosis) is strongly associated with anti-centromere antibody (ACA). Anti-Scl-70 is associated with diffuse cutaneous SSc and pulmonary fibrosis. Anti-RNA Pol III is associated with diffuse SSc and scleroderma renal crisis.

questions.q: A 7-year-old child presents with grouped, itchy, crusted vesicles on the scalp that have developed into multiple tender, boggy, inflamed plaques with purulent discharge and cervical lymphadenopathy. The most likely diagnosis is:
questions.exp: Kerion is a severe, host immune response to a tinea capitis infection, presenting as a boggy, tender, purulent, inflamed swelling with hair loss and lymphadenopathy. It is most often caused by T. verrucosum or T. mentagrophytes. Treatment: oral griseofulvin with systemic steroids to prevent scarring alopecia.

questions.q: A 40-year-old woman undergoes intralesional corticosteroid injection for a keloid. The correct technique and drug of choice for this procedure is:
opts: Betamethasone dipropionate 0.05%, injected in dermis at 2-4 week intervals
Triamcinolone acetonide 10-40 mg/mL, injected intralesionally at 4-6 week intervals
Methylprednisolone acetate 20 mg/mL, once monthly for 6 months
questions.exp: Triamcinolone acetonide (TAC) 10-40 mg/mL is the gold standard for intralesional treatment of keloids and hypertrophic scars. It is injected directly into the lesion (not subcutaneous) at 4-6 week intervals. Side effects include skin atrophy, hypopigmentation, telangiectasia.

questions.q: A 35-year-old HIV-positive patient on HAART (efavirenz-based) develops a widespread maculopapular eruption within 3 weeks of starting therapy, associated with fever and mucosal erosions. The CD4 count rises from 50 to 250 cells/μL. This most likely represents:
questions.exp: IRIS (immune reconstitution inflammatory syndrome) occurs when recovering immunity mounts a paradoxical inflammatory response to previously subclinical or treated infections. It typically occurs within weeks of HAART initiation, with rising CD4 counts. Skin manifestations of IRIS include herpes zoster, Kaposi's sarcoma flare, and molluscum.

questions.q: A patient presents with a painless, firm, subcutaneous nodule on the leg that has been slowly growing over 5 years. Biopsy shows palisading granulomas surrounding necrobiotic collagen with mucin deposition. Fasting blood glucose is 260 mg/dL. The diagnosis is:
questions.exp: Necrobiosis lipoidica (diabeticorum) presents as yellowish-brown, atrophic plaques on the shins in diabetics. Histology shows palisading granulomas around necrobiotic collagen with mucin in the dermis. Strongly associated with DM (up to 65% of cases), though may precede DM diagnosis.

questions.q: A 28-year-old presents with itchy papules on wrists, anterior ankles, and buccal mucosa showing a white lacy Wickham's striae pattern. Lesions are violaceous, polygonal, and flat-topped. The biopsy would most likely show:
opts: Spongiosis with eosinophilic infiltrate in dermis
Band-like lymphocytic infiltrate at DEJ with basal cell degeneration and saw-tooth rete ridges
questions.exp: Lichen planus histology shows: hyperkeratosis, irregular acanthosis, band-like lymphocytic infiltrate at DEJ, basal cell degeneration (vacuolar/liquefaction), Civatte bodies, and saw-tooth rete ridges. DIF shows linear/shaggy fibrinogen at DEJ. The 5 Ps: pruritic, purple, polygonal, planar (flat-topped), papules.
